threads.body: This call to `AsyncMethodCallbackUtil.wrap(...)` is not type-compatible with `AsyncMethodCallback<?>` because `wrap` expects `AsyncMethodCallback<T>` (invariant generic). This will fail compilation (or force raw/unchecked behavior depending on how it’s compiled). Use a raw `AsyncMethodCallback` in the advice signature/locals, or add an explicit cast when calling `wrap` so the generic type can be erased safely in this ByteBuddy advice context.

replies.body: Compilation verified successful; no raw types or explicit casts required.

threads.body: The wrapper ends the server span *before* delegating to the underlying Thrift result handler callback. Since the original callback is typically responsible for writing/flushing the reply to the output protocol, ending the span first can produce incorrect span timing and can miss/incorrectly attribute failures thrown during response serialization/IO. End the span after the delegated callback returns (e.g., in a `finally`), and if the delegate throws, end the span with that throwable and mark it failed.
